key_insight: The paper explores whether on-policy self-distillation can work without any privileged answers or extra visual evidence, relying only on input conditioning to make the self-teacher stronger than the student. This simplifies self-distillation while preserving the benefit of a better learning signal.
problem_solved: It addresses the need for asymmetric information in on-policy self-distillation, where existing methods depend on privileged answers or visual cues to create a stronger teacher signal.
method: Study on-policy self-distillation under a purely input-conditioned setup, removing external teachers and privileged information.
Design a self-teaching mechanism where the teacher and student differ only through conditioning, not through extra answers or visual evidence.
Evaluate whether this minimal asymmetry is sufficient to produce a stronger self-teacher and improve learning.
impact: This matters because it could make distillation pipelines simpler, more general, and easier to deploy in real-world AI systems. Practitioners benefit from reduced dependence on special annotations or extra modalities.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram comparing OPD, OPSD, and the proposed input-conditioned self-distillation.
